Underrepresented in Medicine Variables- URM variable vs URM_AAMC : The URM variable provides higher overall representation of underrepresented in medicine students within the cohort compared to the stricter criteria (URM_AAMC). I suggest we use the URM variable in analysis for preventing small sample size limitations, maintaining adequate statistical power, and allowing for a more robust comparative evaluation.

OSCE Variables-

OSCE: PI mentioned that they are most interested in the Communication and Physical examination OSCE exam scores, these will be treated as primary outcomes. OSCE scores were aggregated across component (communication, physical examination, medical documentation, or oral)

This table above summarizes the missing data analysis, showing the count (n_miss) and percentage (pct_miss) of missing values for various OSCE component scores and exam metrics. Across the listed variables, missingness ranges from 41 to 65 observations, representing roughly 20.6% to 32.7% of the dataset.

This table above evaluates missing OSCE scores at the student level, showing that the majority of students 129 students, or (64.8%) have complete data with zero missing scores. Across the remaining students, missing OSCE counts range from 1 to 16 missing items (16 missing items = all OSCE component scores).

After excluding 39 students who lacked complete OSCE data, the analytical sample for the new dataframe (df_clean) was reduced to a sample size of N = 160.

Table 1 above: Baseline demographic characteristics, standardized examination scores (USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 CK), and OSCE performance metrics were summarized overall and stratified by URM status. Continuous variables are presented as mean (SD) and categorical variables as n (%).

Constructed OSCE variables represent the mean of the Bates, Ramos, Payne, Hyde, and Snelling scores for each evaluation component. For each student, available pre-clerkship OSCE scores were averaged across cases and semesters separately for communication, physical examination, medical documentation, and oral presentation.

Click to expand: Mean Scores with SD by OSCE Exam - not aggregated
Click to expand: Mean Scores with SD by OSCE Exam stratified by URM status - not aggregated

This grouped horizontal bar chart illustrates mean performance across the four aggregated OSCE competency categories (Oral Presentation, Communication, Medical Documentation, and Physical Examination), stratified by URM status. Mean scores and error bar spreads remain closely aligned between URM and non-URM groups across all four domains, with Oral Presentation showing the highest overall averages and Physical Examination recording slightly lower performance.
